run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-16T09:41:25Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate alert for otel-demo/frontend-proxy is backed by real, observed failures: frontend-proxy's `ingress` server spans return HTTP 503 with otel.status_code=ERROR (0.0185 spans/s at 09:45; 89.2 error-span increase over 08:41:25–09:57:25), while no other frontend-proxy operation reports errors. Every captured failing access-log line is `503 UC upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}` with upstream cluster `frontend` and upstream host 100.68.43.111:8080 (the frontend Service ClusterIP), i.e. the frontend side terminated an established upstream connection before sending any response. Causal detail: the failing requests travelled on connections that had just been idle ~5.95–5.99 s (port 34442 last served 200s at 09:40:01.838 then 503 at 09:40:07.791; port 45744 last served 200s at 09:40:34.832 then 503 at 09:40:40.826) while those same connections had served many 200s moments earlier, and the failing traces contain no frontend span at all — the classic keep-alive idle-timeout race between an Envoy upstream pool whose idle timeout exceeds the backend HTTP keep-alive and the backend reaping the idle socket. frontend itself looked healthy on its own signals (0 error spans on all its operations, pod Running/Ready, restartCount 0, serving 200s on other connections at the same seconds), so the alerting service is affected and the frontend is the counterpart of the mismatch rather than a failing workload. Two capacity findings remain as separate, non-proven contributors: frontend runs at ~0.96–1.10 of its 100m CPU limit with 25–39% CFS throttling, and frontend-proxy at ~0.85–0.95 of its 30m limit. A payment Deployment rollout at 09:31:47 was considered and rejected as a cause.

claims.text: At 2026-11-16T09:45:00Z frontend-proxy had a nonzero error-span rate of 0.0185 spans/s, while every other instrumented service except recommendation (0.0037/s) and fraud-detection (0.0037/s) was 0; the whole error rate of frontend-proxy belonged to span_name="ingress" (0.0185/s) with span_name="router frontend egress" at 0 errors/s and 12.87 UNSET spans/s.

The failing spans are frontend-proxy `ingress` spans with status_tags {error:true, http.status_code:"503", otel.status_code:"ERROR"}, each paired with a child `router frontend egress` span carrying {error:"true", http.status_code:"0"} (no upstream response), and the parent load-generator `GET` span also records 503; 8 such ingress errors plus 2 ingress 200s were in the error-trace sample covering 09:10:56–09:24:41.

All 9 captured failure access-log lines of pod frontend-proxy-6b4d584985-sznks between 09:23:24.272 and 09:40:54.351 are exactly `503 UC upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}` with upstream cluster `frontend` and upstream host `100.68.43.111:8080` (the frontend Service ClusterIP); no other 503 form appears in that read.

The 503s occur on reused upstream connections after a ~6 s idle gap: proxy upstream port 34442 served successful 200s from 09:39:45.604 through 09:40:01.838 and then returned `503 UC upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}` at 09:40:07.791 (5.953 s after that last success); port 45744 served 200s at 09:40:34.521/34.582/34.832 and then failed identically at 09:40:40.826 (5.994 s later).

Failing trace 709eb4a032836ed636b37e6da5cb181f contains only 4 spans (load-generator `user_browse_product` and its erroring `GET`, plus frontend-proxy `ingress` and `router frontend egress`); there is no frontend span in it, so nothing shows the request being handled by frontend.

frontend pod frontend-675fd7b5c5-zjtpt is Running and Ready with restartCount 0, empty lastState and container started 08:59:38 (spec limits cpu 100m / memory 200Mi); frontend-proxy pod frontend-proxy-6b4d584985-sznks is likewise Running/Ready, restartCount 0 (limits cpu 30m / memory 50Mi), and all 21 otel-demo pods are Running with 0 restarts.

frontend showed no error signal of its own at 09:45:00Z — all 18 of its instrumented operations report 0 error spans/s (including GET, POST, /api/cart, /api/data, /api/checkout and its gRPC client calls) — and frontend-proxy was serving 200 `via_upstream` requests on other connections in the same seconds as the failures (e.g. successful calls on port 34442 until 09:40:01.838), so a broadly failing frontend is not supported.

frontend container CPU usage/limit is ~0.96–1.10 across 09:13–09:53 with CFS throttling of 0.25–0.39 of periods, while frontend-proxy is at ~0.85–0.95 of its limit with throttling 0.06–0.19; frontend throttling was already ~0.29 at the first sampled point (09:11:25).

frontend-proxy's error rate is sporadic rather than sustained: the 1-minute series over 08:43:25–09:57:25 shows isolated nonzero points (first at ~09:12:25 with 0.0111/s), spikes of 0.322/s at ~09:33:25 and 0.444/s at ~09:34:25, and the total increase of ingress error spans over 08:41:25–09:57:25 is 89.2.

No sample of the frontend-proxy ingress error series exists before ~09:15:00Z: a 15-minute-rate query over the full 24 h authorized window returned only three points (0.00125/s at 09:15, 0.0092/s at 09:30, 0.0874/s at 09:45), so no pre-incident baseline can be established from this metric.

The Kubernetes objects are consistent with the intended wiring: the frontend Service selects opentelemetry.io/name=frontend on port 8080 and has endpoint 100.96.5.121 → pod frontend-675fd7b5c5-zjtpt:8080, and the two relevant ReplicaSets frontend-675fd7b5c5 and frontend-proxy-6b4d584985 were both created 08:59:35 with 1/1 available (no rollout of either during the incident).

The only abnormal-timeline event inside the window for otel-demo is the payment Deployment rollout: ReplicaSet payment-54499f9786 created 09:31:47, old ReplicaSet payment-55766d76b9 scaled to 0 replicas, and pod payment-55766d76b9-846r8 received event `Killing/Stopping container payment` at 09:31:50; no Evicted, OOMKilled, Unhealthy, BackOff or Failed events exist for frontend or frontend-proxy.

The payment rollout at 09:31:47 is not the cause of the frontend-proxy alert: payment reported 0 error spans/s on GET, dns.lookup and tcp.connect at 09:45, its new pod is Running/Ready with 0 restarts, and the 503s are `upstream_reset_before_response_started` against upstream cluster `frontend`, not payment.

Container termination, eviction or OOM on the frontend/proxy pods is not supported: frontend and frontend-proxy have restartCount 0, empty lastState, no OOMKilled/Evicted/Unhealthy events, and both were serving traffic throughout the window.

Primary hypothesis: a keep-alive/idle-timeout mismatch on frontend-proxy's egress path to frontend. The frontend HTTP server reaps idle keep-alive connections after ~5 s, while the proxy's Envoy upstream pool keeps them and reuses them ~5.95–5.99 s after the last response on that socket, so the request hits an already-closed connection and Envoy returns 503 with detail `upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}`; without a retry policy for these requests the error surfaces as the alert. This explains the UC detail, the ~6 s idle gaps, the absence of any frontend span for the failed requests, and why other connections served 200s in the same seconds.

Secondary hypothesis (contributing, unproven): frontend is CPU-saturated at its 100m limit (usage/limit ~0.96–1.10, 25–39% of CFS periods throttled), which delays its keep-alive timers and event loop and widens the close/reuse race; proxy log lines also show individual request times climbing to 500–1204 ms in the same period. It cannot be the sole cause because frontend reported no error spans and served many 200s concurrently with the failures.

Third hypothesis (capacity, unproven): frontend-proxy itself runs at ~0.85–0.95 of its 30m CPU limit with 6–19% throttling, which could add proxy-side delay; however the observed failure detail attributes every 503 to the upstream resetting the connection (UC / connection_termination), not to proxy-side overflow or connect failure (no UO/UF response flags were observed).

Align the frontend-proxy egress keep-alive configuration with the frontend's HTTP keep-alive: set the Envoy upstream cluster http_protocol_options idle_timeout (and any upstream keep-alive settings) clearly below the frontend's keepAliveTimeout, or raise the frontend server keepAliveTimeout well above the proxy idle timeout, and add a retry policy for safe/idempotent requests on upstream resets to absorb the residual race.

Re-size the two CPU-limited containers: raise the frontend limit above 100m (sustained usage equals the limit with 25–39% throttling) and frontend-proxy above 30m (~0.9 of limit), then re-check whether the 503 rate and the multi-hundred-ms latency spikes persist; also reconcile frontend memory (working set 229–248 MiB against a reported 200Mi limit) to rule out memory-driven stalls.

gaps: The frontend-proxy Envoy configuration could not be read: no ConfigMap matching frontend-proxy|envoy exists in otel-demo (only 4 ConfigMaps there, none matching), so the actual upstream idle_timeout / keep-alive and retry settings are unverified and the mismatch is inferred from observed timing, not from configuration.

The RequestErrorRate alerting rule is not present in the registered Prometheus rule set (list_prometheus_rules for rule_name=RequestErrorRate returned no_data), so the rule expression, threshold and denominator behind the annotated 0.0222 value are unverified.
No samples of traces_span_metrics_calls_total for frontend-proxy exist before ~09:15:00Z inside the 24 h authorized window, so the pre-incident baseline and the exact onset of the 503s are unknown.

Metric and log counts do not agree: the span metric reports an 89.2 increase in ingress error spans over 08:41:25–09:57:25 and a 0.32/0.44 per-second burst at ~09:33–09:35, yet a complete log read of 09:32:00–09:36:00 (9508 lines, read limit not reached) contains only one 503 line, so neither the exact error count nor that burst is established.
The frontend container produced no readable log lines in the incident window (fetch_pod_logs returned no_data), so server-side close/error messages of the frontend HTTP server could not be inspected.

No HTTP server latency metric was available for frontend (http_server_request_duration_seconds_count had no series in the window), so frontend response-time distribution could not be measured directly.
The Endpoints objects report readiness as null for the frontend and frontend-proxy addresses, so endpoint readiness at the incident time was not verified.
The change_history integration is not available in this Run, so no record of deployments or configuration edits (e.g. keep-alive/timeout or resource changes) preceding the alert could be checked.
next_steps: Read the deployed Envoy bootstrap/cluster configuration of frontend-proxy (image-baked file or its source manifest) and compare upstream http idle_timeout, connection pool and retry policy against the frontend server keepAliveTimeout.

If the frontend is a Node.js/Next.js server, inspect its configured keepAliveTimeout/headersTimeout values and set them longer than the proxy's upstream idle timeout (or shorten the proxy idle timeout below them).
After the keep-alive alignment, re-check the frontend-proxy ingress 503/UC rate over at least an hour and confirm the ~6 s idle-gap pattern disappears.
Confirm the RequestErrorRate rule definition and threshold in Alertmanager/Prometheus so the annotated 0.0222 value is understood, and consider a short retry policy for idempotent routes.

Evaluate raising frontend CPU (currently 100m, sustained at limit with 25–39% throttling) and frontend-proxy CPU (30m, ~0.9 of limit), and reconcile frontend memory working set against the 200Mi limit.
